steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Muslims must pray five times a day (salah) — at dawn (Fajr), midday (Zuhr), afternoon (Asr), evening (Maghrib) and night (Isha). This is the second Pillar of Islam and the most frequent daily religious practice.

steps.title: RS Exam Tips — Salah: Prayer
steps.body: 1. For Salah: Prayer questions, always include specific scriptural or source references where relevant 2. Explain both religious and non-religious viewpoints 3. Use specialist vocabulary precisely (e.g. terms from the specification) 4. Evaluate by analysing strengths and weaknesses of different views before reaching your conclusion 5. Link your discussion of Salah: Prayer to its real-world impact on believers and society

steps.title: UK Context
steps.body: In the UK, many mosques organise their five daily prayers around work and school schedules. The East London Mosque, one of the busiest in Europe, hosts over 7,000 worshippers for Friday Jummah prayers. During Ramadan, attendance increases significantly, with many British Muslims making a special effort to attend mosque regularly.

steps.title: UK Context
steps.body: In British mosques, Sunni and Shi’a communities generally worship separately due to these differences in prayer practice, though they share many other aspects of Islamic life. In universities and workplaces, British Muslims of both traditions may pray together, adapting their practice to the shared space and time available.

steps.title: Try it yourself
steps.body: Explain two Muslim practices during salah.

steps.title: Check your answers
steps.body: 1) Wudu — before prayer, Muslims perform ritual washing (ablution) of hands, mouth, nose, face, arms, head and feet. This purifies the body and symbolises spiritual cleanliness before approaching Alla

steps.title: Exam tips
steps.body: Always refer to specific sources of authority (scripture, sacred texts, religious leaders) Explain contrasting beliefs — different views within and between traditions Use key terminology precisely (e.g. tawhid, atonement, sanctity of life) For 12-mark evaluation questions, consider both sides before reaching a justified conclusion Link beliefs to their impact on individuals, communities and society Acknowledge diversity — no religious tradition has a single, uniform view
